title: Aiming
text: The carriage rattled and jolted.
“So we’re still traveling even at night… I wonder if there are any monsters around?”
Just as I thought that, the carriage came to a stop. We were on a mountain road on the way to the next town.
“Huh? What’s going on?”

My father peered out from between the stopped carriages. A messenger clad in a robe stepped down from the carriage and approached my father… drawing his sword and spear as he drew near. Sensing the danger, my father’s face turned pale as he realized what was happening.
“You fell for it, you fool.”
“You were looking so carefree, weren’t you? Seriously, the King should’ve just done this from the start instead of making things so complicated.”
“He didn’t want to arouse the suspicion of the other Heroes, did he? It’d be a real pain if they got on guard, wondering when they’d be killed, and ended up running away.”
“Wha… uh… s-so, is this what Motoyasu was talking about!?”
“It’s too late now, Shield Hero! Brace yourself!”
I’ve got to get there in time!
“Lightning Spear!”

I hurled a lightning-charged spear at those trying to kill my Father. A flash of light, like a bolt of lightning unleashed from the unshakable strength forged by the enhancements the future heroes had taught me, flew toward Melromarc’s assassins.
“Gyaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!”

Crackling lightning took shape and pierced the enemies. However, I hadn’t yet managed to defeat all of them. Meanwhile, I ran toward the carriage, determined to protect Father even a little bit. At the same time, the spear returned to my hand.
“It’s been a while since I’ve used this.”
I focused my consciousness on the spear and locked onto the enemies with a skill that has high accuracy but lacks power.
“Aiming Lancer X!”

I threw the glowing spear with all my might. Aiming Lancer. Back when this was just a game, it was a skill that granted a high accuracy bonus. Its damage was mediocre—only slightly stronger than the Air Strike Javelin. You could call it a guaranteed-hit move… though, of course, that wouldn’t hold true if it were knocked out of the air by a parry or the like. But with my current strength, taking out the lot of them trying to kill my Father is a piece of cake.
“Guaaaaaaaaaaaah!”
“Waaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!”

The spear, radiating an aura, pierces through the enemies I’ve targeted. Thanks to its multi-lock function, it flies toward every enemy I’ve targeted. There were three enemies. I took out one with the Lightning Spear and two with the Aiming Lancer.
“Father! Are you okay!?”
I rush over to the carriage and call out to my Father.
“Y-You’re Motoyasu… yeah. I’m… fine, but…”
Stepping down from the carriage, my Father stares at the fallen enemies.
“D-Did you kill them?”
“It wasn’t a situation where I could hold back.”

True, I could have taken them alive and forced them to reveal who the mastermind was, but if I’d done that, my Father might have been killed. If that had happened, we’d be right back where we started.
“Why would an envoy from Siltvelt…”
“No, that’s not it. He wasn’t an envoy from Siltvelt—he was either a soldier from Melromarc or a follower of the Three Heroes Church.”
“The Three Heroes Church?”
“It’s the state religion here, but it’s a radical faction… a group that you, Father, drove to ruin in the future.”
“I-I see. Motoyasu… you saved me, didn’t you? Thank you so much.”
“There’s no need to thank me. It’s my duty, after all.”
Just as we were deeply moved by this emotional reunion, Éclair caught up with us, looking completely exhausted.
“I finally… caught up…”
“You are…?”

My father looked at Éclair’s face and asked, his cheeks flushing slightly. She certainly isn’t a pig… which is a sign that she possesses both stunning beauty and a kind heart. Well, compared to Filo-tan, she might as well be a pig, though.
“My name is Eclair Seaetto. For certain reasons, I’m accompanying Lord Kitamura, and I’ve rushed here to assist the Shield Hero.”
“Is that so?”
“Shield Hero, that was a close call. If Lord Kitamura, the Spear Hero, hadn’t been there, who knows what would have happened by now…”
“Yeah, I know that all too well… So what Motoyasu-kun said was true, after all.”

My father has finally come to believe in me. In that case, I suppose I should tell him everything that’s happened so far. Just as I was thinking that, my father began to explain what had transpired up to that point.
“Princess Malty told me that the envoy from Siltvelt had arrived earlier than expected, so I had to leave. And even though everyone came to see me off, I never imagined it would turn out like this…”
My father looks very sad.
“Father, please don’t be sad. I, Motoyasu, and this Éclair are here for you.”

“No, I… I’m fine for now. “That’s right—I’ll do my part to support the Shield Hero as well. Since I’m in this country anyway, I should head to either Siltvelt or Shieldfreeden, where they’ll take good care of the Shield Hero.”
“Yeah… That’s the golden rule of battle. Melromarc tried to pull this stunt because they didn’t want me to go to either of those two countries, so I’m not about to just take it lying down.”
“That’s exactly the kind of Father you are.”
“Haha, for some reason, I’m starting to get used to being called ‘Father’ by Motoyasu-kun. Nice to have you around, once again.”
And so, we succeeded in rescuing my Father. However, the very next day, wanted posters for the two of us were distributed throughout the country… well.
“I think the most important thing right now is to cross the border.”
It was the morning after we’d spent the night outdoors… Eclair said that.
“That’s true… but I’m hungry.”

We hadn’t eaten properly yesterday, and it had been one battle after another. Normally, we would’ve eaten at the cafeteria, but I’d been trapped underground, and Father had left immediately by carriage. In other words, we hadn’t eaten a single meal since arriving in this world. When I think about it that way, Father’s words make perfect sense.
“Well, let’s put eating aside for now. What should we do next?”

Right now, we have absolutely no money or equipment. Thanks to my level and my enhanced spear, I can fight, but we definitely need equipment and money. With our current financial situation, we can’t even afford to buy Filolial-sama’s egg. Plus, both Father and I are in our street clothes.
“If they catch up to us, we can escape using the Portal skill.”
“I suppose so…”
“I guess we have no choice…”
Yesterday, Éclair stripped the armor from the corpse of a soldier we’d left behind. It seemed to weigh on her mind, and looking at the stolen money pouch, Father said to Éclair:
“Did you end up feeling bad about stealing from the dead after all?”
“No… Stripping a dead person of their belongings goes against my code of chivalry, but given the circumstances, it couldn’t be helped.”
Let’s try saying something my Father might say.

“There are no rules on the battlefield. If you can survive on chivalry alone, then by all means, do so. But right now, we’re doing just fine to stay alive… Protecting yourself is also important—is dying heroically really what chivalry is all about?”

“That’s a tough one to hear. You’re right. On the battlefield, you have to step forward and fight, even if it means stepping over the corpses of your comrades. And as for confiscating the belongings of those who tried to kill Lord Iwatani with such underhanded tactics… I suppose that’s something we have to compromise on.”
“To feel such revulsion even at the idea of taking from the enemy… You’re a very principled person, Eclair. That’s pretty cool.”
“L-Lord Iwatani. Being ‘cool’ isn’t something to aspire to. Even I’ve had to resort to acting like a night thief when I had no other choice.”
“Let’s stave off our hunger with the monsters we encounter along the way. As for money… it seems we have a little bit, so we’ll just have to buy whatever we need along the way.”
“Yeah. That’s right.”
“Mm-hmm.”
And so we set off. In a village along the way, we confirmed a public notice warning that a dangerous criminal armed with a shield and spear and a former knight of the kingdom were roaming the area.
“Hmm…”
I looked at the sign from a distance and thought it over.
“Motoyasu, what are you thinking about?”
“They’re getting pretty annoying, so I’m thinking about going out and killing that Trash, that Crimson Swine Bitch, and the Pope of the Three Heroes Church.”
“Wha!?”
“L-Lord Kitamura, if you do something like that, you’ll be wanted all over the world. Please bear with me for a little while longer.”

Since the two of them stopped me, I grit my teeth and hold back. For now, we’ve decided to quietly continue our journey. The carriage that Father was riding in doesn’t have a single scratch, so we’re using it as is. Assuming we don’t use Filolial-sama to get to Siltvelt, it’ll probably take three or four weeks by carriage. It feels like it’s taking a bit too long, though… But then again, the portals I currently possess only lead to nearby locations.
“We don’t get any EXP even when we defeat monsters, do we?”
“That’s because of the repulsion between heroes.”
“Come to think of it, you did mention something like that. Is this what you meant?”
“If I step away, you’ll be able to gain EXP… but then we might not be able to respond to sudden emergencies.”

Every now and then, national soldiers or adventurers attack us, as if they were our pursuers. My Father waits in the carriage while I mow them down. It’s the third day heading toward Siltvelt… The memory of slaying yet another assassin is still fresh in my mind.
“It’s dangerous. Lord Iwatani is only Level 1. But this country is far too dangerous to level him up here, and I’m not confident I can protect him on my own.”
Ah, I miss Filolial-sama. I miss his fluffy, glossy, healthy feathers.
“It would be reassuring if we had at least a few more companions…”
“Can we trust them?”
Father replies to Éclair with a skeptical look.
“That’s the problem…”
It certainly is a tough one. We can’t tell friend from foe. Come to think of it… it’s about time the envoy from Siltvelt makes contact. That said, we’re currently wanted criminals.
Just as I was thinking that, a familiar Demi-Human and two pigs walked straight toward us. That’s impressive. To think they’ve tracked down our location… Éclair drew her sword and went on high alert.
“I… am an envoy from Siltvelt. I am the last remnant of Seaetto… Please sheathe your swords. We have no intention of fighting.”
“Hmm… All right.”
The envoy bowed deeply to my Father, as if in prayer, before beginning to speak.
“Shield Hero, Spear Hero, would you please come to our country?”
“We were actually planning to head to Siltvelt anyway…”
My father mutters under his breath, looking away as if the words were hard to say.
“I almost got killed by people posing as envoys from Shiltvelt, so I can’t trust them… Motoyasu, I want to ask you—do you think we can trust these people?”

Last time, my father died because he entrusted himself to these very people. Since the exact reason remains unclear, I can’t completely rule out the possibility that they’re imposters posing as envoys.
“You mentioned the future, didn’t you?”
“Yeah. That’s why it’s dangerous.”

During our journey so far, I’d explained to my Father that we were stuck in a loop. I’d told him everything without holding anything back—including the fact that he died after I entrusted him to those people claiming to be envoys from Siltvelt.
“I offer my deepest condolences that the Shield Hero’s journey has been a series of deceptions. It pains me deeply that I cannot trust you.”
“That’s exactly it. I’d like to believe you if I could…”
But everything that’s happened so far makes it impossible to believe them. At the very least, here in Melromarc, there are probably very few people we can trust.
“In that case, I think you should just make us slaves and keep us under lock and key.”
“Slaves… That’s certainly one option.”
“Slaves… You mean… In this world, slaves are bound by a slave mark and can’t disobey their master’s orders, right?”
“That’s correct.”
“I see… but slaves, huh?”
Éclair’s face clouded over. Seeing that expression, my Father spoke up, looking flustered.
“Sorry, Ms. Éclair. I think we should be extra careful just to be on the safe side.”
“I know. We must proceed with the utmost caution—as if we were checking every stone before crossing a bridge.”
“What about the enslavement ritual? If we have an inkwell, I think we should be able to enslave them, don’t you?”
“I’ll have it prepared. Please wait a moment.”
“Just to be safe, I’d like to register as your master as well—is that all right?”
“If that’s the condition for your trust, I’ll gladly accept it.”
I stepped forward to survey the area. A few hours later… an envoy from Siltvelt brought the inkwell to us.
“Father, you need to drop a small amount of blood into this inkwell.”
“U-uh, okay.”
My father lightly cut his fingertip with Éclair’s sword and let a drop of blood fall into the inkwell. Then I, too, let my blood flow into the inkwell.
“Next, we’ll go to the nearest collaborator who can perform the ritual, and we’ll become slaves. Please wait here.”
And so, we hid in a sparsely trafficked forest and waited for the envoy from Siltvelt to enslave us. Eventually, a slave icon appeared in our field of vision.
“Whoa, is this the slave status screen? There are all sorts of options here.”
“That’s right. Now we just need to check the precautions—like not lying on the form, not showing hostility toward our master, and not attacking—before we join them.”

I set everything up and explained it to my Father. If anything, I’m better at registering monster crests, but there isn’t much of a difference. Still, the fact that they’re properly enslaving people means they’re not fakes… I suppose that’s a safe assumption, right?
